claims.text: In situ TEM can elucidate mechanistic aspects of oxidation in additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
EDS coupled with in situ TEM can elucidate oxidation-induced elemental redistribution of nanoprecipitates in this alloy.
The initial additively manufactured alloy contains dual nanoprecipitates.
In situ TEM during high-temperature oxidation can provide real-time observation of changes in nanoprecipitate size.
In situ TEM during high-temperature oxidation can provide real-time observation of changes in nanoprecipitate distribution.
EDS can quantify oxidation-induced changes in nanoprecipitate composition.
The additively manufactured alloy will exhibit a 20% lower oxidation rate, measured by weight gain per unit area, than cast and wrought counterparts of the same nominal composition.
The reduction in oxidation rate will correspond to increased elemental redistribution within the nanoprecipitates.
TEM sample preparation may limit the proposed analysis.
Electron-beam exposure may create artifacts during the in situ TEM experiment.
EDS quantification is subject to uncertainty in the proposed experiment.
